national_raw_news.content: India and New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) will come into force from tomorrow on the occasion of Vijay Dashami. The agreement will provide duty-free access for 100 per cent of Indian exports to New Zealand. Addressing the ceremony marking the entry into force of the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement in New Delhi today, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that the agreement is aligned with the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi for Viksit Bharat 2047. He said, the agreement opens significant new opportunities for India’s exporters, particularly MSMEs, artisans, farmers and pharma. The Minister highlighted that both the countries have agreed to work towards the goal of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services with New Zealand to approximately 35 thousand crore rupees by 2030. Mr Goyal said that India’s farmers will gain wider market access for fruits, vegetables, spices and other agricultural produce. He said, the agreement will help improve productivity, support higher incomes and strengthen livelihoods. The Minister highlighted that sensitive sectors, including dairy, remain protected, keeping farmers’ welfare at the heart of the government’s approach. The Minister said that New Zealand’s commitment to facilitate 20 billion US dollars in investment into India holds immense potential to strengthen manufacturing, infrastructure, services and innovation. Mr Goyal said, this agreement will also create employment opportunities. He expressed confidence that this win-win partnership will achieve many more milestones, guided by the shared vision of growth and mutual prosperity between the two nations. The FTA between India and New Zealand was signed in April this year at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The Agreement will create new opportunities in services, investment and professional, student and youth mobility, including enhanced pathways for Indian professionals and students. India and New Zealand share longstanding and close relations, anchored in strong people-to-people ties and expanding cooperation across trade and investment, agriculture, education, sports, technology and other areas. The Bilateral merchandise trade between India and New Zealand stood at around 1.1 billion US dollars in 2025-26. The FTA represents a significant step in further strengthening these ties and creating new opportunities for businesses and communities in both countries. On the occasion, the first-ever export of a JCB machine from India to New Zealand was flagged off by the Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal. Flag-offs of a range of products across the agriculture, gems and jewellery, engineering, sporting goods, footwear and leather sectors are also planned for the entry-into-force day. These initiatives reflect the confidence of Indian manufacturers and the opportunities the Agreement opens up for exporters across the country.

national_raw_news.title: India receives record FDI inflows of over $748 billion between 2014 and 2025 4 hours ago 63
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through the FDI Policy. India’s foreign direct investment policy has undergone major reforms over the past decade, with the government liberalising sectoral rules to attract greater foreign investment into the country. The government has progressively liberalised FDI norms in key sectors, including defence, telecommunications, insurance and space. Foreign investment of up to 74 per cent is permitted in defence, 100 per cent in telecom, insurance and Space sector. The country has received a record over 748 billion US dollars in FDI between 2014 and 2025. The number of source countries investing in India also rose from 89 to 112. Addressing the Rozgar Mela in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted that today more than one hundred countries are investing in India through FDI. Chief Economic Advisor V. Anantha Nageswaran said that India has opened up several sectors, including space, drones, defence and insurance, to foreign investment. The FDI policy reforms reflect India’s efforts to create a more investor-friendly environment, simplified investment procedures and to strengthen its position as a preferred global investment destination.

national_raw_news.title: President Murmu congratulates Rinku and Ajeet Singh on javelin gold and silver at Asian Para Games 2026 3 hours ago 36
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated para athlete Rinku on winning the Gold Medal and Ajeet Singh on winning the Silver Medal in the Men’s Javelin F46 event at the Asian Para Games 2026. The President said that Rinku’s throw has carried the Indian Tricolour to the top of the podium and brought immense pride to the nation. She said that this achievement will inspire aspiring javelin throwers to aim farther. The President also congratulated Soumya on winning the Gold Medal and Radha Venkatesh on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s 1500m T12/13 event. She expressed hope that they will continue to pursue their sporting goals with full confidence, and will get many more opportunities in the future to showcase their talent on the track. President Murmu has also extended her wishes to Nishad Kumar on winning the Gold Medal in the Men’s Long Jump T47 event. She said that this remarkable success highlights his versatility and willingness to take on new challenges. The President also congratulated Ravi K. Budigina on securing the Silver Medal in the Men’s 100m Freestyle S13 at the Games. She wished that this achievement will inspire aspiring swimmers to take the plunge and pursue their ambitions with conviction. She also congratulated Kokila on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s Judo J2 -52kg category and Kapil Parmar on winning the Bronze Medal in Para Judo at the Games. She said that this success will inspire them to continue striving for excellence and reach even greater heights in their sporting journey. President Droupadi Murmu also congratulated Mona Agarwal on winning the Gold Medal in the Women’s 10 meter Air Rifle Standing SH1 event at the Asian Para Games 2026. In a social media post, the President appreciated the efforts of the athlete for setting a new Asian Para Games record. She also expressed confidence that her achievement will inspire many to dream big. President Murmu also emphasised that even the most ambitious dreams can be realised with determination and hard work. She also congratulated Avani Lekhara on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s 10m Air Rifle Standing SH1 event at the Games. President Murmu wished her best for the future and expressed hope that her sporting journey will continue to provide her with new opportunities to excel and fulfill her aspirations.

national_raw_news.title: Manipur Police celebrates 135th Raising Day in Imphal 2 hours ago 25
national_raw_news.content: The 135th Raising Day of Manipur Police was celebrated today at 1st Battalion Manipur Rifles Parade Ground in Imphal. The celebration was attended by Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh, Speaker of Manipur Legislative Assembly- Thokchom Satyabrata Singh, Home Minister- Govindas Konthoujam, MLAs, DGP, Chief Secretary and high ranking police officers. Since 2008, Manipur Police has celebrated 19th October as the collective Raising Day of Manipur Police of the entire Manipur Police family. This year, various sports and other events were organised across the State as run-up events for the grand celebration held today. A total of 13 contingents participated in the March Past in today’s celebration while the Chief Minister presented various awards to outstanding battalions, police stations and police personnel for their exemplary performance and dedication to duty. Addressing the celebration, the Chief Minister said that around three thousand acres of illegal poppy cultivation has been destroyed, three hundred and seven cases have been registered under NDPS Act and four hundred sixty seven drug traffickers have been arrested in the last one year in the State. Shri Khemchand said that the Government is committed to combating illegal poppy cultivation and drug trafficking in the State and police and other concerned agencies have been closely monitoring the situation and intensifying efforts to identify, trace and dismantle drug networks operating across the State. The Chief Minister said that the crisis erupted on May 3, 2023 have led some youths to take up arms, however the State Government in coordination with the security force efforts to promote peace, reconciliation and a return to normalcy in the State is ongoing. He appealed to all sections of society and all political parties in the State to foster a culture of appreciating good deeds and pointing out wrongdoings with a view to rectifying them. Shri Khemchand emphasized that undue criticism would only further undermine the progress of the State and would in no way contribute to the restoration of peace in the State.

national_raw_news.title: India and Saudi Arabia discuss bilateral electrical interconnection initiative - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: India and Saudi Arabia discuss bilateral electrical interconnection initiative Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर India and Saudi Arabia discuss bilateral electrical interconnection initiative ANI | Updated: Oct 20, 2026 03:50 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 20 (ANI): Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Power, held a virtual bilateral meeting with Nasser Al-Qahtani, Assistant Minister of Energy for Electricity Affairs, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, to review the progress of the India–Saudi Arabia Electrical Interconnection initiative and explore avenues for strengthening cooperation in the power sector. The discussions focused on the progress of the proposed electrical interconnection between India and Saudi Arabia, which holds significant potential to deepen bilateral energy cooperation. Both sides exchanged views on the way forward and underscored the importance of sustained engagement to advance the initiative. The two sides also explored opportunities to broaden cooperation in other areas of mutual interest in the power sector, with an emphasis on technical collaboration, knowledge sharing and the exchange of best practices. The Saudi Arabian side expressed interest in enhanced cooperation in the areas of Extra High Voltage (EHV) transmission systems, addressing technical and operational challenges associated with higher penetration of renewable energy in the grid, strategies for accommodating the growing power requirements of emerging data centres, and updating grid codes to address evolving power system requirements. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining constructive dialogue to further deepen the India–Saudi Arabia partnership in the power sector. On the other hand, India has advised its nationals residing in Saudi Arabia to exercise due precautions, move to the nearest safe place in the event of an aerial attack, and strictly refrain from filming, publishing or sharing any information, photos or videos regarding the ongoing events. "The Indian community in Saudi Arabia is advised to take due precautions under the prevailing situation. In case of an aerial attack, immediately proceed to the nearest safe place (inside a building or an interior room away from windows), and refrain from filming, publishing, or sharing any information, photos, or videos related to the ongoing events," the Indian Embassy posted on X. Embassy officials have continued visiting hospitals where Indian nationals are receiving medical care while remaining in constant communication with their families to provide necessary support. Flight operations remain suspended at Riyadh's international airport, while Dammam, Jeddah and Medina airports remain operational despite ongoing disruptions. Indian carriers have halted flight services to and from Saudi Arabia, with the Embassy outlining alternative travel options. "Indian carriers have extended the suspension of flights to and from Saudi Arabia, as outlined below: Air India, Air India Express, Indigo -- until Oct 24, on all routes. Akasa Air -- until Oct 27, on all routes," it posted on X. "Some available flight options are outlined below: Saudia: Scheduled flights to India from Dammam, Jeddah and Medina. Flynas: Dammam-Delhi and Dammam-Mumbai flights (Oct 17-24); scheduled Dammam-Lucknow services continue. Flyadeal: Dammam-Mumbai flights on Oct 17-18," it added.
